series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "The INDC of Bangladesh consists of the following elements: Mitigation contribution: An unconditional contribution to reduce GHG emissions by 5% from Business as Usual (BAU) levels by 2030 in the power, transport and industry sectors, based on existing resources. A conditional 15% reduction in GHG emissions from BAU levels by 2030 in the power, transport, and industry sectors, subject to appropriate international support in the form of finance, investment, technology development and transfer, and capacity building. A number of further mitigation actions in other sectors which it intends to achieve subject to the provision of additional international resources. Adaptation component: An outline of what Bangladesh has already done on adaptation and what the next steps are, including the long-term vision for adaptation in Bangladesh and synergies with mitigation measures. INDC implementation: Proposals for governance and coordination of INDC implementation and an outline of key next steps. Support for INDC implementation: A qualitative description of Bangladesh's support needs and an outline of plans to further quantify this, along with some examples of indicative costs of taking action on mitigation and adaptation."
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 5% (unconditional) to 15% (conditional) reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU levels
ndc_assessment.gases: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6
ndc_assessment.sectors: Power sector, energy use in the transport and industry sectors
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

evidence.sentence: Bangladesh submitted its Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) to UNFCCC on 25 September 2015 with an ambitious GHG reduction target of 15% from a Business as Usual (BAU) level by 2030.
The full implementation of the National SLCP Plan is expected to reduce black carbon emissions by 40% and methane emission by 17% in 2030 compared to a business as usual scenarios.
Contingent upon international funding and technological support, the country targeted to reduce GHG emissions in the same sectors up to 36 MtCO2e by 2030 or 15% below BAU emissions.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is NDC 3.0, filed 2025-09-29. 49 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (3). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 292.4 MtCO₂e, DS-35 241.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 0 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 37.0 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 5% (unconditional) to 15% (conditional) reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared to the BAU levels It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.15°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.99°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
